parts.summary: The comments from Rollins & Sumrall Education Group highlight Mississippi's success in improving educational outcomes while heavily relying on E-Rate funding and technology investments. The group supports the idea that higher levels of E-Rate support are associated with improved educational outcomes.

The text discusses the impact of E-Rate support on educational outcomes in Mississippi, noting improvements in academic performance after implementing the program. It mentions Mississippi's achievement gains in reading and math, particularly in fourth-grade math, which improved from No. 49 to No. 16 between 2013 and 2024. The text also highlights the state's initiatives to provide digital learning resources and support to schools through the Mississippi Connects program funded by E-Rate.

The comment discusses the importance of E-Rate funding for broadband infrastructure and services in Mississippi, highlighting the positive impact on student outcomes and the need to maintain the program.
The comment opposes sunsetting the E-Rate program as a statutory authority.

claims.argument: The comment opposes sunsetting the E-Rate program as a statutory authority.

parts.summary: Mississippi school districts face budget cuts and reduced funding for E-Rate programs due to declining enrollment and new school funding formulas. Districts with small budgets must maintain complete networks in every school, despite having no in-house IT staff. The district in West Bolivar was forced to cancel its requests for managed internal broadband services in both years, despite having no in-house IT staff.
